facts.fact: Dhanu is a hill route-keeper who sends runners to Kunal and is paid in cut-corner silver; his runner is an unnamed boy.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Kunal pay Dhanu's runner and the runner report Raghu.

facts.fact: Chuni, nine, is a scullery girl in Garh Neshar's kitchen passage.
facts.why: needed because the private-face beat requires a child for Kunal to teach.

facts.fact: Sarn fold is a high pasture where a shepherd saw Captain Raghu.
facts.why: needed because the report of Raghu in the high hamlets needs a place detail.

facts.fact: The hill council meets in the hall of Garh Neshar under the brass bell; Old Bhim speaks for the lower terraces.
facts.why: needed because the council scene needs a location.

facts.fact: Ila's own covering note said only 'every way'; the crown's formal cover sheet addressed to the council carries the extra clause about the way beneath the Shilak Cairn, which she has not seen.
facts.why: needed to reconcile ch 1's short commission with the clause read aloud in ch 2.

facts.fact: Captain Raghu fled last winter's Snow Fair (Book 1's Fair) with a dozen loyalists and has been in hiding since.
facts.why: needed because the beat says he fled the Fair and ch 1 places this Fair a year later.

facts.fact: The Shepherd's Stair route-song is a child's counting rhyme ('One for the goat who knows the gate, two for the stone that will not wait...') that ends 'nine and thirty and the ghosts go by'; Kunal teaches it as nonsense so it can be carried unrecognised.
facts.why: needed for the private-face beat and clue C10; the thirty-nine echoes the tower stair count in ch 1.
